author: Daniel J. Dillberg
gate: EXP-406 Ghost #17 — EMA lag-overshoot=1.033; tail variability at N=20; 2-cycle not fully broken
description: Adaptive alpha_bze schedule: alpha_eff(n)=alpha_min+(alpha_max-alpha_min)*exp(-n/tau_alpha). High inertia during bistable crossing (n<5, alpha~0.9), decays to light inertia post-convergence (n>>tau, alpha->0.2). Both tau_alpha and tau_warmup synchronized at 5.0. Ghost #17 lag-overshoot bounded by initial high-alpha damping; fast tracking restored at large n.
pipeline: mu -> L_tau -> [phi_fb_adaptive_ema(bze_ema_prev, scene_n) -> B_tau] -> R_tau -> Z -> S -> W -> OBS
schedule_sync: tau_alpha == tau_warmup == 5.0. alpha_min=0.7 > alpha_crit=0.667: guaranteed 2-cycle suppression at all n. alpha_max=0.9: initial freeze. alpha range 0.9->0.7 (narrow): refined inertia modulation over warmup only.

ghost_notes.Ghost_17: EXP-406 EMA lag-overshoot=1.033 from fixed alpha=0.5 carrying momentum past beta_raw peak. EXP-407 adaptive alpha: high alpha during rising phase prevents lag accumulation; low alpha after convergence allows faster tracking.
ghost_notes.Ghost_18_candidate: If alpha_eff decays too fast (tau_alpha too small), system may enter EXP-404-like transient overshoot after alpha drops to alpha_min. Monitor overshoot_ratio vs EXP-404.
ghost_notes.Ghost_18: Alpha_min=0.2 (original) drops below alpha_crit=0.667 at large n, reintroducing 2-cycle. Fix: alpha_min=0.7 > alpha_crit ensures persistent 2-cycle damping at equilibrium. Revised EXP-407 uses alpha_min=0.7, alpha_max=0.9.

assertions.A3_stronger_damping: bze_407[1] < bze_406[1] (alpha=0.9 at n=1 vs alpha=0.5)
